opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full_time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed. Max for full_time without owning role is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin to Source Code, which exceeds max of read. Recommend read.
reason: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requested admin to Source Code. The two team notes conflict on employment status: one records full_time (max write, since Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code), while the Security DB records contractor with basic training (max read; write requires advanced training, admin never allowed). Given the contradictory records, the conservative and safer maximum is read. Since admin exceeds the maximum under either reading, I grant the maximum supported by the more restrictive (and lower) record: read.
